scope.reason: The full chain is now linked: Express registration, CommonJS constructor handler, positional-callback continuation, captured Mongo collection, AND the request-to-filter dataflow — GET /allocations/:userId reads `allocations` with filterOrigins [params.userId, query.threshold]. What remains is the severity class of the matching rule and a false-positive ownership signal.

label.criterion: The upstream source labels the session-user alternative as the fix for insecure DOR; the live code instead trusts the URL parameter.
label.why: displayAllocations reads req.params.userId and queries allocations for it, even though the caller is only checked as logged in.

missCause: One cause, precisely located. The G1 half was fixed: a client-supplied value no longer builds an ownership assertion (`callAssertsOwnership`). Its TWIN remains — `whereOwnerScoped` reads the filter `{userId: <identifier>}` as an owner scope without asking where the value came from, so the route still carries `ownerScoped` and the advisory stays suppressed. Even unsuppressed, OBJECT_SCOPE_UNPROVEN is advisory: true by design (ADR-058) and can never be a hard finding. Route recognition, handler linkage, async linkage, the DB effect and the request-to-filter dataflow are ALL modelled. The route stays UNKNOWN.
